Mynkivtsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Mynkivtsi's Jewish community, present from the first half of the 17th century, perished during the Khmelnytsky massacre; in 1757, Talmud books belonging to Mynkivtsi's Jews were confiscated and burned in the square at Kamyanets-Podilskyi — the same episode of the Jacob Frank controversy documented at Derazhnya and Orynyn elsewhere in this collection — and Sabbatean and Frankist ideas spread locally. In 1796, the first printing house in all of Podolia opened in Mynkivtsi. The Jewish population peaked at 2,196 (67 percent of the town) in 1897. On August 30, 1941, 2,200 Jews were executed, and the remnants of the community were deported to the Dunaivtsi ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection.
